In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XylB enzyme is not suitable to be used in the xylitol production process, since it is able to produce the toxic xylitol-phoshate.
the use of XylB in E. coli strains for xylitol production is not recommended, due to its toxic xylitol-phosphorylating activity.
XylB is not the best choice for xylulokinases in xylose fermentations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Xyl3 can be used to produce high xylitol concentrations from xylose in E. coli.
Xyl3 from P. stipitis can functionally replace XylB from E. coli, but that it does so with less toxicity.

the use of P. stipitis xylulokinases (Xyl3) in engineered E. coli is a promising strategy for xylitol production from xylose, and may have broader applications in the engineering of microbial xylose utilization.

the XYL3 gene is an attractive alternative to xylB in the production of xylonates and xylitol from xylose.
